quotes.text: The fundamental difference isn't encryption or storage. It's the consent model. One empowers you to curate, the other defaults to indiscriminate archiving.

quotes.text: While Vision doesn't retain photos or video, the text transcript of your interaction can remain in your chat history, something you control and can delete at any time.

quotes.text: Memory is intentionally opt in and auditable. Recall is automatic device local screenshots, and vision is session based analysis where text transcripts may persist.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the three consent models side by side.

chapters.title: What Copilot Memory is and isn't
Privacy controls for users and admins

takeaways: Copilot Memory only stores what users explicitly ask it to remember, shows a memory updated badge and can be reviewed, edited or switched off.
Windows Recall on Copilot+ PCs captures encrypted local screenshots automatically, so enterprises need to assess it separately for compliance.
Admins can disable memory for a tenant or groups and audit memory actions through Microsoft Purview eDiscovery.
hook: Many users fear that Copilot is quietly recording everything they do, and they often confuse Copilot Memory with Windows Recall and Copilot Vision. This episode is for end users, admins and compliance teams who need to explain the difference. It walks through what each feature keeps, how consent works and which controls you can use today.
